key_insight: Jointly training subgrid-scale and wall closures inside a differentiable CFD solver captures their coupled effects better than fitting either closure alone.
engineering_relevance: The framework improves wall-modeled LES accuracy and transferability across Reynolds numbers, meshes, and domains, making it promising for practical turbulent-flow simulation.
method: Differentiable hybrid neural--CFD solver for end-to-end training
Two composed closures: neural network + fixed differentiable conventional layer
Low-order statistics used as training targets for joint SGS and wall closure optimization
evidence_signal: In posteriori tests on a turbulent boundary layer from Re_theta = 600 to 6500, the model outperformed WMLES baselines, generalized beyond the training Reynolds range, and reproduced mean profiles and energy spectra without directly training on spectra.
watch_item: The approach depends on differentiable solver integration and joint training, so implementation complexity and solver/optimization stability may be significant in new CFD codes.
paper_title: Differentiable Hybrid Neural-CFD Modelling of Wall-Bounded Turbulence: Coupled Learning of Subgrid-Scale and Wall Closures
